title: Alignment Artifact Strength sets the minimum alignment an actor needs to act correctly when using an Artifact
content:
A.0.1.1.6 defines the strength of an Alignment Artifact as the **minimum level of Universal Alignment an actor must possess** in order to take universally aligned actions when interacting with it.

This reframes institutional design as raising a floor rather than selecting for virtue. A weak Artifact only produces good outcomes when handled by highly aligned actors; a strong one produces good outcomes even from poorly aligned ones.

Strength is increased "by ensuring that Ecosystem Intelligence evolves such that each actor's self-interested incentives correspond as precisely as possible with requirements of Universal Alignment." The closer that correspondence, the less **Inner Incentive** — extra effort to overcome misalignment — an actor must supply from their own character.

The design consequence is testable: to strengthen an Artifact, reduce the gap between what is profitable and what is right, rather than exhorting participants to be better.
description: A stronger Artifact demands less Inner Incentive: strength is raised by making self-interested incentives coincide with what Universal Alignment requires.
